newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice prices firm, heavy Iraq offtake.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice prices firm, heavy Iraq offtake.

text.p: Thai rice prices firmed this week on buying from Japan, Nigeria and substantial offtake from Iraq, trade sources said on Thursday.
Two ships were loading almost 40,000 tonnes of 10-15 percent grade rice for delivery to Iraq, they told Reuters.

A senior commerce ministry official told Reuters earlier that Baghdad has bought 390,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand so far this year and was expected to buy more. About 80,000 tonnes had been delivered.
Japan held a rice tender recently in which it bought 39,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand for July and August shipments, official and traders said.
Of the total, 28,500 tonnes were 100 percent grade B rice and 10,500 tonnes broken rice, they said. Price details were not available.
Nigeria also entered the market this week to buy a moderate amount of parboiled rice for nearby shipment, traders said.
Thai benchmark 100 percent B grade rose to around $340-365 per tonne FOB Bangkok while 100 percent fragrant rice also edged up to $710-725 per tonne on the same basis.
"The prices edged up due to strong demand while supplies were dwindling at the end of season," said one trader.
"However, some exporters and shippers have already covered their postions. We expect rice to trade around the current level with an upward bias," he added.
